record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: When Lindstedt series fail to be analytic in the non-analytic KAM setting, determine whether some broader notion of summability, such as Borel summability, still holds.

evidence.quote: In more general cases where the summability of Lindstedt series may fail it is an open question to know if some extended notion of summability, like Borel summability (quite frequent in quantum field theory), may still hold.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a nearly integrable Hamiltonian system of the form
H(I, φ; ε) = H_0(I) + ε V(I, φ),
where (I, φ) ∈ ℝ^d × 𝕋^d are action–angle variables, H_0 is real-analytic and anisochronous (det ∂²H_0/∂I² ≠ 0), V is a perturbation, and ε ∈ ℝ is a small parameter. For an unperturbed frequency vector ω = ∂H_0/∂I(I_0), the Lindstedt series is the formal power series in ε whose coefficients describe an invariant torus carrying quasi-periodic motion with frequency ω.

In the classical KAM setting where ω is Diophantine and V is analytic, the Lindstedt series converges and defines an analytic invariant torus. There are, however, more general "non-analytic KAM" regimes — e.g. weakly Diophantine or resonant frequency vectors, lower regularity of V, or degenerate situations — in which the Lindstedt series is known (or believed) to diverge, while the corresponding invariant torus is at best C^∞ in ε.

Problem. In such non-analytic KAM regimes where the Lindstedt series fails to be (analytically) summable, determine whether the formal Lindstedt series is nevertheless Borel summable (or summable in some other extended sense, e.g. multisummable, Gevrey-summable, or summable via a generalized Borel-type transform) to the actual invariant torus / quasi-periodic solution as a function of ε.
artifact.category_tag: KAM theory and Lindstedt series summability
artifact.status_search_result: Borel summability of Lindstedt series has been established in several specific non-analytic KAM-type settings: Costin, Gallavotti, Gentile and Giuliani proved Borel summability for resonant invariant tori in two-dimensional cases with Diophantine exponent τ=1 (e.g. golden-mean frequency ratio), and related Borel summability results exist for strongly dissipative quasi-periodically forced equations. However, the general question — whether some extended notion of summability such as Borel summability holds in arbitrary non-analytic KAM settings where the Lindstedt series diverges — remains open.

status_evidence.title: Borel summability and Lindstedt series
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for Borel summability of resonant Lindstedt series are found for two-dimensional rotation vectors with Diophantine exponent τ=1 (e.g. golden mean).
status_evidence.claim: Borel summability of the Lindstedt series is established in a specific non-analytic KAM setting (resonant tori, 2D, τ=1).

status_evidence.title: Summation of divergent series and Borel summability for strongly dissipative differential equations
status_evidence.snippet: Borel summability is shown for divergent series arising in strongly dissipative quasi-periodically forced ODEs.
status_evidence.claim: Related Borel summability results exist for nearby perturbative problems with quasi-periodic forcing.

status_evidence.title: KAM Theory in Configuration Space and Cancellations in the Lindstedt Series
status_evidence.snippet: Cancellation mechanisms in the Lindstedt series are analyzed beyond the standard analytic KAM framework.
status_evidence.claim: The general non-analytic KAM regime is still under active investigation, with no fully general summability theorem known.
